qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Amcor benefits from packaging converting scale and customer qualification switching costs on high-speed filling lines, but lacks economic pricing power over inflation. Contractual resin pass-through mechanisms pass raw material costs with a multi-month lag without expanding conversion margins. 10-year median GAAP ROIC is ~8.5%, consistently failing the 12% threshold across the business cycle. Mega-acquisitions (Bemis in 2019, Berry Global in 2025) dilute returns on capital rather than deepening an economic moat.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC = 8.5% < 12%, REJECT). Amcor operates as a high-volume packaging converter structurally squeezed between petrochemical resin oligopolies and concentrated consumer staples brand owners. 10-year median GAAP ROIC of ~8.5% sits well below the 12% hurdle across the cycle. Dilutive mega-mergers (Bemis, Berry Global) create asset bloat without demonstrating economic pricing power above inflation.
qualitative.evidence: 10-year median GAAP ROIC of ~8.5% (FY20: 7.6%, FY21: 10.1%, FY22: 8.8%, FY23: 10.5%, FY24: 9.1%, FY25: 5.7%). Amcor is a price-taking converter between resin producers (Dow, ExxonMobil, LyondellBasell) and multinational FMCG customers (Nestlé, PepsiCo, P&G, Coca-Cola). Contractual resin pass-through clauses protect nominal dollars with a lag but fail to deliver real conversion margin pricing power. The April 2025 Berry Global merger substantially expands balance sheet debt and goodwill without lifting structural returns on capital.
